node.title: Re: Perl code inside the Mojo::Template
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
First of all, I would very strongly recommend against using [mod://CGI].pm when you have [mod://Mojolicious] available. Just use Mojo for everything! Update: I showed a code comparison between CGI.pm and Mojo in [id://11131500|this node], and I have a bunch of Mojo examples [id://830550|on my scratchpad]. /Update

% if($n->{'year'} eq <%= $number %> ) {

A line beginning with % is Perl code, and <%= $number %> is not valid Perl code. Try "% if($n->{'year'} eq $number ) {" instead.

ALso is it possible to use a sub routine from the Perl code inside the template?

Yes, you can use subroutines, though you usually need to import them into the template's namespace with a use statement or similar, by calling them by their full name (in your case main::name_val, though I personally find this a little ugly), you can change a template's namespace via the namespace option (though as the [mod://Mojo::Template|documentation] says, be careful), or when using templates as part of a larger Mojo app, by installing them as a "helper" (see [mod://Mojolicious]).

% name_val(<%= $n->{'name'} %>) %

Same problem here, try "<%= main::name_val( $n->{'name'} ) %>" instead.
